tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
The recorded steps log into Magento Admin, navigate to the Manage Customers grid, and exercise all relevant controls: ID range filter (From/To), name and email text filters, customer group dropdown, telephone and ZIP text filters, country dropdown, state text filter, customer since date range (From/To), website dropdown, Search and Reset Filter buttons, the View-per-page selector and pagination (next page), and an Edit link to navigate to a specific customer detail page.

Task Definition:
Create a reusable tool that, starting from an already-authenticated Magento admin browser session, navigates directly to the Manage Customers grid, applies any subset of the available filters, triggers a Search, optionally adjusts pagination (page size and page number/next), and then returns the resulting grid contents including Edit links. It must robustly interact with the previously fragile Reset Filter button by using a more reliable selector or an agent step.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate directly to the Manage Customers grid URL.
2) (Optional but deterministic) Close the "Incoming Message" overlay if present, so it does not block controls.
3) Input filter values into the filter row fields: ID range From/To, Name, Email, Group select, Telephone, ZIP, Country select, State/Province, Customer Since From/To, Website select. Only populate fields for which input parameters are non-empty.
4) Click the Search button to apply filters and wait briefly for the grid to reload.
5) Optionally change the page size (View per page) if a page-size parameter is provided, then click Search or rely on automatic reload.
6) Optionally navigate pagination if a page number is specified, using the page number input box; otherwise remain on current page.
7) Extract the customer grid: visible row data (ID, Name, Email, Group, Telephone, ZIP, Country, State/Province, Customer Since, Website) and per-row Edit link URLs.
8) If requested, click Reset Filter to clear all filters and restore default grid (using a robust agent step for Reset Filter, given past deterministic failures), then re-extract the grid.

Variable Identification:
Based on actual field names/behaviors in Magento 1.9 Manage Customers grid, the key technical filter parameters are:
- entity_id[from], entity_id[to] for ID range.
- name for Name filter.
- email for Email filter.
- group_id for Customer Group dropdown.
- telephone for Telephone filter.
- postcode for ZIP filter.
- country_id for Country dropdown (expects ISO country code or special value for All Countries).
- region for State/Province text filter.
- customer_since[from], customer_since[to] for date range (format MM/DD/YYYY).
- website_id for Website dropdown.
Additionally for pagination:
- limit (page size, via View per page select) and page (current page input/selector).
We also may want a boolean to indicate whether to perform a Reset Filter before applying new filters.

Step Optimization:
- Navigation: go directly to /index.php/admin/customer/; no need to simulate menu clicks.
- Deterministic interactions: use CSS selectors with form field names/ids where known and stable, not highlight indices. However, this tool schema must rely on the controller’s generic selectors (cssSelector) because we only recorded element hashes. We'll map them to the known Magento names/ids in cssSelector.
- Reset Filter previously failed when using a generic semantic selector like button[title='Reset Filter'] in tests. In the recorded session, the Reset Filter button consistently appeared as a <button> element with a unique title attribute. However, the failure log from prior attempts indicated that selector sometimes failed to resolve. To address this, we:
  * Use an agent step to click the Reset Filter button by visible text "Reset Filter" instead of relying solely on a deterministic selector. This makes the step resilient to minor structural changes.
- Search button interactions were reliable; we can use a deterministic selector based on title="Search".
- The ID, name, email, telephone, ZIP, state, and date range fields can be targeted by input[name='...'] selectors which are stable in Magento.
- Group, Country, Website, and View-per-page controls can be targeted by select[name='...'] selectors.
- We keep the tool single-purpose: apply filters and return grid data. We do not automate exporting, mass actions, or editing a specific customer beyond providing Edit links in the output.

Because this JSON tool format does not support conditional branching, we will:
- Always navigate to the customer grid URL.
- Always perform Reset Filter first via an agent step to ensure a clean slate; this is acceptable because Reset is safe and idempotent.
- Always fill each filter field with provided parameter values; if the parameter is an empty string, the caller should omit it or pass an empty value to mean "no filter".
- Always click Search after setting filters.
- Optionally adjust page size and page number based on parameters; if parameters are empty, the underlying selectors will still be interacted with but given the default values passed through (we can pass the current value). To keep the tool simple, we will treat page_size and page_number as optional inputs and only change them when provided (non-empty) via their parameters.

Given the previous Reset Filter deterministic-selector failure, we explicitly implement Reset Filter as an agent step "Click the 'Reset Filter' button on the Manage Customers grid" instead of a deterministic click.

Input schema summary:
- entity_id_from (string, optional) -> ID From
- entity_id_to (string, optional) -> ID To
- name (string, optional) -> Name filter
- email (string, optional) -> Email filter
- group_id (string, optional) -> Customer Group visible label
- telephone (string, optional) -> Telephone filter
- postcode (string, optional) -> ZIP filter
- country_id (string, optional) -> Country visible label (e.g., "United States")
- region (string, optional) -> State/Province filter
- customer_since_from (string, format MM/DD/YYYY, optional)
- customer_since_to (string, format MM/DD/YYYY, optional)
- website_id (string, optional) -> Website visible label (e.g., "Main Website")
- page_size (string, optional) -> View-per-page option ("20","30","50","100","200")
- page_number (string, optional) -> Desired page number ("1", "2", ...)

Steps will:
1) navigation -> /index.php/admin/customer/
2) agent -> click "Reset Filter" button
3) input/select_change on all relevant filters using cssSelector with corresponding field names
4) click Search button deterministically
5) adjust page size if given and click Search again
6) adjust page number if given and hit Enter on the page input
7) extract_page_content of the grid to structured output (customers list with Edit links).

This addresses previous failures by:
- Using an agent step specifically for Reset Filter instead of a brittle deterministic selector.
- Using stable name-based selectors for all filter fields and Search.
- Avoiding reliance on highlight indices or ambiguous class-only selectors.
name: tool_search_customers_v5
description: Search Magento customers in admin grid using flexible filters (ID range, name, email, group, telephone, ZIP, country, state, customer-since date range, website) plus pagination, then return the resulting customer grid including Edit links.

steps.description: Open Magento Admin Manage Customers grid page.
Use agentic reasoning to reliably trigger the Reset Filter button, avoiding brittle deterministic selectors that previously failed.
steps.task: On the Magento Manage Customers grid page, click the 'Reset Filter' button in the Actions area above the grid to clear all current filters and restore the full customer list.

steps.description: Wait for the grid to reload after Reset Filter is applied.
Set ID range lower bound filter (From). Leave empty string if no lower bound is desired.
Set ID range upper bound filter (To). Leave empty string if no upper bound is desired.
Set Name filter.
Set Email filter.
Select Customer Group filter option by visible text.
Set Telephone filter.
Set ZIP/Postcode filter.
Select Country filter option by visible text.
Set State/Province filter.
Set Customer Since start date (From) in MM/DD/YYYY format.
Set Customer Since end date (To) in MM/DD/YYYY format.
Select Website filter option by visible text.
Click the Search button to apply all configured filters.
Wait for filtered customer grid to reload.
Adjust 'View per page' page size selector if a value is provided.
Set desired page number in pagination input if provided.
Trigger pagination change by pressing Enter in the page number input.
Wait for the grid to reload after any pagination changes.
Capture the resulting customer grid and Edit links after filters and pagination are applied.
steps.goal: From the Magento Manage Customers grid page, extract the full customer table rows currently visible, including columns ID, Name, Email, Group, Telephone, ZIP, Country, State/Province, Customer Since, Website, and the URL behind each row's 'Edit' link, in structured JSON format.

input_schema.name: entity_id_from
input_schema.description: Lower bound of customer ID range filter (maps to input[name='entity_id[from]']). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: entity_id_to
input_schema.description: Upper bound of customer ID range filter (maps to input[name='entity_id[to]']). Leave empty to ignore.

input_schema.name: name
input_schema.description: Customer name filter text (maps to input[name='name']).

input_schema.name: email
input_schema.description: Customer email filter text (maps to input[name='email']).

input_schema.name: group_id
input_schema.description: Visible label of Customer Group to filter by, e.g. 'General', 'Wholesale', 'VIP Member', 'Private Sales Member' (maps to select[name='group_id']).

input_schema.name: country_id
input_schema.description: Visible label of country to filter by, e.g. 'United States' (maps to select[name='country_id']).

input_schema.name: customer_since_from
input_schema.description: Customer Since start date in MM/DD/YYYY (maps to input[name='customer_since[from]']).

input_schema.name: customer_since_to
input_schema.description: Customer Since end date in MM/DD/YYYY (maps to input[name='customer_since[to]']).

input_schema.name: website_id
input_schema.description: Visible label of Website to filter by, e.g. 'Admin' or 'Main Website' (maps to select[name='website_id']).

input_schema.name: page_size
input_schema.description: Number of records per page (View per page selector).

input_schema.name: page_number
input_schema.description: Customer grid page number to navigate to, e.g. '1', '2', '3' (maps to page number input).
